name: Function Analysis (TRIZ)
description: Components, interactions and function model – the starting point for the other TRIZ tools
whenToUse: When a technical system is to be broken down component by component to find harmful, insufficient and excessive functions and to spot trimming candidates by value and cost — not for a contradiction that is already named; the contradiction matrix and the physical contradiction cover that.

confirm.deleteUsed: Delete "{name}"? {count} function(s) use it and will be deleted too.
confirm.deleteUsedUnnamed: Delete "(unnamed)"? {count} function(s) use it and will be deleted too.

invariants.uniqueComponentIds: Every component needs its own non-empty id; positions in the function model belong to existing components.
invariants.singleTarget: There is at most one target.
invariants.validPairs: A pair links two different existing components, sorted (a < b) and only once; a ticked pair is not excluded at the same time.
invariants.uniqueFunctionIds: Every function needs its own non-empty id; label positions belong to existing functions.
invariants.functionEnds: Carrier and object of a function are existing components or empty, and never the same component.
invariants.levelByType: A useful function has a level (adequate, insufficient, excessive), a harmful one has none (null).

vc.emptyComponents: Add system components in the Components tab.
vc.emptyCosts: Enter costs for the system components in the Components tab.

targetDemoted: "{name}" is now a system component – there is only one target.
matrixEmpty: Add at least two components on the "Components" tab.
pairLocked: Used by {count} function(s) – delete those functions first.
noFunctions: No functions yet. Click an open pair.
addOnPair: Add another arrow on this pair
noDisadvantages: No disadvantages – all functions are useful and adequate.
